neighborhoods.name: St. George
neighborhoods.summary: St. George is Staten Island's civic and cultural hub, anchored by the iconic Staten Island Ferry terminal and sweeping views of the Statue of Liberty and Lower Manhattan skyline. A walkable neighborhood with Victorian homes, new waterfront development, and growing arts scene, it offers average prices around $350 per square foot.

faqs.question: What is the average home price in St. George?
faqs.answer: The median sale price in St. George is approximately $475,000. Victorian single-family homes range from $400,000 to $750,000, while newer condos near the waterfront can range from $350,000 to $600,000. Per square foot pricing averages around $350.

faqs.question: How do you get from St. George to Manhattan?
faqs.answer: The Staten Island Ferry provides a free 25-minute ride from the St. George Ferry Terminal to Whitehall Terminal in Lower Manhattan. It runs 24/7, with departures every 15-20 minutes during rush hours and every 30 minutes off-peak. The St. George SIR station also connects to the rest of Staten Island.

faqs.question: Is St. George a good neighborhood for commuters?
faqs.answer: Yes, St. George has the best transit access on Staten Island. The free Staten Island Ferry connects directly to Lower Manhattan, and the St. George terminal is the northern terminus of the Staten Island Railway. Express bus routes (SIM1, SIM15) also run to Midtown.

faqs.question: What is the St. George waterfront development?
faqs.answer: The St. George waterfront has undergone significant revitalization including Empire Outlets (New York City's first outlet shopping center), the National Lighthouse Museum, and new residential developments. The area continues to attract investment with mixed-use projects along the esplanade.

faqs.question: What types of homes are available in St. George?
faqs.answer: St. George offers a diverse housing stock including Victorian-era single-family homes on the hillside with harbor views, newer waterfront condos and rentals, multi-family rowhouses, and a small number of co-ops. The hilltop homes above the ferry terminal are particularly sought after for their panoramic views.

faqs.question: How much is rent in St. George?
faqs.answer: Median rent in St. George is approximately $1,800 per month for a one-bedroom. Studios average $1,400, two-bedrooms $2,200, and three-bedrooms $2,800. Newer waterfront developments command a 15-20% premium over older housing stock.

neighborhoods.name: Todt Hill
neighborhoods.summary: Todt Hill is the highest point on the Atlantic seaboard south of Maine, known for its grand estate homes, lush landscaping, and serene residential atmosphere. One of New York City's most affluent neighborhoods, it offers sprawling properties with average prices around $525 per square foot.

faqs.question: What is the average home price in Todt Hill?
faqs.answer: The median sale price in Todt Hill is approximately $1,050,000. Estate-style homes range from $800,000 to $3 million or more, while smaller homes and attached properties can start around $650,000. Per square foot pricing averages around $525.

faqs.question: What makes Todt Hill special?
faqs.answer: Todt Hill is the highest natural point on the eastern seaboard south of Maine, rising 409 feet above sea level. The neighborhood is known for its grand estate homes set on large lots, mature trees, and winding roads. It also borders the 2,800-acre Staten Island Greenbelt, the largest contiguous natural area in New York City.

faqs.question: How do you commute from Todt Hill?
faqs.answer: Todt Hill is car-dependent. Most residents drive to the nearby SIR stations (Grant City or Old Town) or use express bus routes (SIM1, SIM4) to Manhattan. The drive to the St. George Ferry Terminal is about 15 minutes. The Staten Island Expressway provides access to the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.

faqs.question: Are there good schools in Todt Hill?
faqs.answer: Yes, Todt Hill is served by well-regarded public schools including PS 36 J.C. Drumgoole. The area also has proximity to several private schools. The Staten Island Academy, one of the borough's top private schools, is located nearby.

faqs.question: What types of homes are in Todt Hill?
faqs.answer: Todt Hill is primarily single-family detached homes, many on oversized lots with extensive landscaping. Architectural styles include Colonial, Tudor, Mediterranean, and Contemporary. Some properties feature gated entrances, pools, and multi-car garages. The neighborhood also has a small number of townhomes.

faqs.question: Is Todt Hill a good investment?
faqs.answer: Todt Hill has historically maintained strong property values due to its limited inventory, large lot sizes, and desirable location. Homes tend to hold value well and appreciate steadily. The neighborhood appeals to buyers seeking space and privacy that is rare elsewhere in New York City.

neighborhoods.name: Great Kills
neighborhoods.summary: Great Kills is a family-oriented South Shore neighborhood known for its beach access, marina, and tight-knit community character. With Great Kills Park offering 580 acres of beaches and trails along Raritan Bay, and a lively Hylan Boulevard corridor, the neighborhood averages around $425 per square foot.

faqs.question: What is the average home price in Great Kills?
faqs.answer: The median sale price in Great Kills is approximately $625,000. Single-family detached homes range from $500,000 to $900,000, while semi-attached and attached homes can start around $400,000. Per square foot pricing averages around $425.

faqs.question: What parks and schools are near Great Kills?
faqs.answer: Yes, Great Kills is one of Staten Island's most popular family neighborhoods. It has well-regarded public schools, youth sports programs, a marina for boating, and Great Kills Park with beaches and playgrounds. The neighborhood has a strong community feel with active civic associations.

faqs.question: What is Great Kills Park?
faqs.answer: Great Kills Park is a 580-acre unit of the Gateway National Recreation Area managed by the National Park Service. It features beaches along Raritan Bay, nature trails, fishing areas, ball fields, and a model airplane field. Crooke's Point within the park offers scenic waterfront walks.

faqs.question: How do you commute from Great Kills?
faqs.answer: The Great Kills SIR station connects to the St. George Ferry Terminal (about 25 minutes). Express buses (SIM5, SIM8) run directly to Manhattan. The neighborhood has easy access to Hylan Boulevard and the Korean War Veterans Parkway for driving to the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.

faqs.question: What types of homes are available in Great Kills?
faqs.answer: Great Kills primarily features single-family detached and semi-attached homes, many built in the 1950s-1980s. Cape Cods, raised ranches, and split-levels are common styles. Newer construction includes larger colonial-style homes. The area near the marina also has some waterfront properties.

faqs.question: How much is rent in Great Kills?
faqs.answer: Median rent in Great Kills is approximately $1,600 per month for a one-bedroom. Studios average $1,200, two-bedrooms $1,900, and three-bedrooms $2,500. Rental inventory is limited as the neighborhood is predominantly owner-occupied single-family homes.

neighborhoods.name: New Brighton
neighborhoods.tagline: Historic Grandeur on the North Shore
neighborhoods.summary: New Brighton is one of Staten Island's most architecturally distinguished neighborhoods, featuring grand Victorian and Italianate homes along tree-lined streets with views of the Kill Van Kull. Close to the ferry, the Snug Harbor Cultural Center, and a growing arts community, it offers average prices around $375 per square foot.

faqs.question: What is the average home price in New Brighton?
faqs.answer: The median sale price in New Brighton is approximately $525,000. Victorian single-family homes range from $450,000 to $850,000, while multi-family properties can range from $550,000 to $1 million. Per square foot pricing averages around $375.

faqs.question: What is Snug Harbor Cultural Center?
faqs.answer: Snug Harbor Cultural Center and Botanical Garden is an 83-acre campus of 28 historic buildings, including the Chinese Scholar's Garden, the Staten Island Children's Museum, and the Noble Maritime Collection. Originally a home for retired sailors, it is now one of NYC's premier cultural destinations.

faqs.question: Is New Brighton close to the ferry?
faqs.answer: Yes, New Brighton is adjacent to St. George and the Staten Island Ferry Terminal. Most locations in New Brighton are a 10-15 minute walk or a 5-minute bus ride to the ferry, making it one of the best-connected neighborhoods on Staten Island for Manhattan commuters.

faqs.question: What types of homes are available in New Brighton?
faqs.answer: New Brighton features a varied housing stock including grand Victorian and Italianate single-family homes, multi-family brownstones, Craftsman bungalows, and some newer infill construction. The neighborhood is known for architecturally significant homes, many dating to the mid-1800s.

faqs.question: Is New Brighton a good area for the arts?
faqs.answer: Yes, New Brighton has a thriving arts community anchored by Snug Harbor Cultural Center. The neighborhood hosts regular gallery openings, studio tours, and cultural festivals. Several working artists live in the area, and the Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art is located at Snug Harbor.

faqs.question: How much is rent in New Brighton?
faqs.answer: Median rent in New Brighton is approximately $1,700 per month for a one-bedroom. Studios average $1,300, two-bedrooms $2,100, and three-bedrooms $2,600. Multi-family homes offer some of the most affordable rental options, especially garden-level and upper-floor units.

streetGuidance.description: New Brighton's residential streets climb from the waterfront along the Kill Van Kull up to the Brighton Heights ridge. The higher streets offer stunning water views and the grandest homes, while the lower streets near Snug Harbor provide a walkable village atmosphere.
